description: The //stable-staker-v2-cutover:broadcast doc key and the Phase 7 NatSpec claim the breaker stays live at every Phase 7 halt point. At halt 5 (after v2.unpause(), before Pauser.register(V2)) V2 is unpaused but not yet registered, so a committed global Pauser.pause() succeeds yet leaves V2.paused() == false. Containment holds because all three V2 strategies are Pauser-registered and pause: stake/withdraw/autoAnnihilate revert EnforcedPause (0xd93c0665) and claim reverts "claim disabled" (0 succeeding user entry points). The intuitive remedy, a direct V2.pause(), reverts onlyPauser; the working remedy is V2.setPauser(OWNER) then V2.pause(). This is the residual one-tx window left by the L-05 (fc44ca36) fix, not an incomplete fix of it. The audit's own test_P7_everyHaltPoint probe scored k=5 LIVE because it checks only registered contracts (MR-34-SSV2C-04).
impact: No value path: zero V2 user entry points succeed under a global pause at halt 5. The harm is an operator relying on documented breaker coverage during an emergency and finding V2 unpaused, with the obvious remedy reverting.
attackPath: 1. Phase 7 halts after V2.unpause() and before Pauser.register(V2) (halt 5).
2. An emergency coincides; operator calls Pauser.pause() relying on the documented guarantee.
3. V2.paused() stays false; the intuitive direct V2.pause() reverts onlyPauser; correct remedy is V2.setPauser(OWNER) then V2.pause().
